title: Use 224x224 input size
context: All images are 512x512. Need a fixed size for the neural network.
reasoning: 224x224 is the standard for ResNet/EfficientNet pretrained on ImageNet. Using their native resolution avoids mismatched feature scales. We lose pixels but classification depends on style, not fine detail.
outcome: Works fine, no signs that resolution is a bottleneck.

title: Stratified 70/15/15 split with class weights
context: Dataset is imbalanced: 336 (Dali) to 1,322 (Van Gogh) images per artist.
reasoning: Stratified splits keep each artist proportional in train/val/test. Class weights penalise errors on rare classes more, so the model doesn't just ignore minority artists.
outcome: Split: 9,337 / 2,002 / 2,001. Weights range from ~0.6 (Van Gogh) to ~2.0 (Dali).

title: Start with a baseline CNN before transfer learning
context: Need a reference point to see how much pretrained models actually help.
reasoning: 3-block CNN (32->64->128) with GAP and dropout. Standard filter doubling pattern. If transfer learning can't beat this, it's not worth the complexity.
outcome: 48.2% test accuracy -- well above random (4.3%) but clearly limited.

title: Choose ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0 for transfer learning
context: Need pretrained models to compare against baseline.
reasoning: ResNet50: deep (50 layers, 25.6M params), skip connections help with vanishing gradients, very well-studied for transfer learning. EfficientNetB0: much smaller (5.3M params), uses compound scaling. Two different approaches give a meaningful comparison.
action: Implemented both with frozen base -> fine-tuning two-phase approach.
outcome: ResNet50: 78.8% | EfficientNetB0: 73.9%. ResNet wins, probably because it has 5x more parameters.

title: Two-phase training: frozen base then fine-tuning
context: Transfer learning models can be used as fixed feature extractors or fine-tuned.
reasoning: Phase 1 (frozen, lr=1e-4): the new head starts random, so if we unfreeze everything the noisy gradients would mess up pretrained features. Let the head learn first. Phase 2 (fine-tune, lr=1e-5): unfreeze last ~30% of layers. Early layers have generic features that are fine as-is. 10x lower LR to avoid breaking what the model already knows.
action: Freeze base for 30 epochs (lr=1e-4), then unfreeze last ~30% for 15 epochs (lr=1e-5).
outcome: Fine-tuning improved ResNet by +4pp (77%->81% val), EfficientNet by +2pp. ResNet showed 11pp train-val gap though.

title: Try stronger augmentation
context: ResNet50 fine-tuned: 92% train vs 81% val = 11pp gap. Overfitting.
reasoning: More augmentation should help regularise. Random crops force the model to handle partial views, saturation/hue shifts help with colour reproduction differences.
action: Added random crop (85-100%) + resize, random saturation (0.8-1.2), random hue (+-0.02) on top of existing flip/brightness/contrast.
outcome: ResNet50 v2: still 78.8%. Train-val gap actually got worse (12.8pp). The random crop seems to hurt -- cropping destroys composition and composition matters for painting style.

title: Upgrade EfficientNetB0 to B2
context: B0 got 73.9% vs ResNet50's 78.8% despite fine-tuning.
reasoning: B0 only has 5.3M params vs ResNet's 25.6M. Probably just too small for 23 artists. B2 has ~9.2M params, should help.
action: Replace B0 with B2. Keep 224x224 for fair comparison.
outcome: B2: 76.1% (B0 was 73.9%). Better, but still behind ResNet. Train-val gap is only 3.6pp though vs ResNet's 12.8pp -- B2 generalises better.

title: Extend fine-tuning to 25 epochs
context: EfficientNetB0 was still improving at epoch 15.
reasoning: 15 epochs might not be enough. EarlyStopping (patience=5) will stop it anyway if it converges, so extra epochs are safe.
outcome: Completed, need to check if EarlyStopping triggered early.

title: Add label smoothing (0.1)
context: Models are very confident on wrong predictions.
reasoning: With 23 classes and subjective style boundaries (e.g. Picasso's early classical vs late surrealist periods), hard 0/1 targets push the model to be overconfident. Label smoothing (targets become 0.9/0.004 instead of 1/0) acts as regularisation.
outcome: Applied to both models. Should help calibration.

title: Ensemble ResNet50 v2 + EfficientNetB2
reasoning: ResNet uses skip connections, EfficientNet uses squeeze-excitation blocks -- they focus on different things and make different errors. Averaging softmax outputs should cancel out some individual mistakes.
action: Average softmax predictions of ResNet50_v2 + EfficientNetB2.
outcome: 80.5% -- best result so far. +1.7pp over best single model.

title: CutMix augmentation
context: Class imbalance (Van Gogh 1,322 vs Dali 336) and similar Impressionist styles (Monet, Pissarro, Sisley) need softer decision boundaries.
reasoning: CutMix (Yun et al. 2019) pastes a patch from one image onto another and mixes labels proportionally. This implicitly oversamples rare classes and trains with soft targets. Alpha=1.0 (uniform cut sizes). Needs one-hot labels + CategoricalCrossentropy. Applied at batch level via tf.py_function.
action: Implemented cutmix.py with build_dataset_cutmix(). Using ResNet50 as base to isolate the CutMix effect.

title: Add ViT-B/16 as third model
context: All models so far are CNNs (local filters). Painting style often depends on whole-canvas composition and spatial relationships.
reasoning: ViT (Dosovitskiy et al. 2021) splits the image into 16x16 patches and uses self-attention to model relationships between all patches at once. Pretrained on ImageNet-21k (bigger than ImageNet-1k used by ResNet/EfficientNet). Architecturally very different from CNNs, so its errors should be different too -- good for the ensemble.
action: Implemented vit_model.py using TF Hub (sayakpaul/vit_b16_fe/1). Same head and two-phase training as the other models.
outcome: ViT frozen test accuracy: 79.5%. Fine-tuning skipped (86M params on CPU = ~12h/epoch). Frozen ViT still competitive for the ensemble.

title: Test-Time Augmentation (TTA)
context: Paintings in the dataset come from different scanners/cameras with different lighting and colour profiles.
reasoning: Average predictions over 5 gently augmented views of each test image. Only flip + small brightness/contrast (+-5%). No crops -- we showed in decision #6 that crops hurt for paintings. Costs 5x inference time but no extra training.

title: Per-class weighted ensemble (3 models)
context: Phase 2 ensemble used equal weights, but different models are better at different artists.
reasoning: Weight each model per class based on its validation accuracy for that artist. Normalise so weights sum to 1 per class. The ensemble then automatically relies more on whichever model is strongest for a given artist.
action: Implemented ensemble_weighted.py. Both equal-weight and per-class-weighted 3-model ensembles will be evaluated.
outcome: Per-class weighted: 83.4%. Equal-weight: 83.2%. Weighted beats equal by 0.2%.
